# aeneid-079 drafter notes (X.606–688)

38 units. Title `Imago Aeneae. Turni fuga`; part "The Phantom of Aeneas (X.606–688)"; titleEn "The Phantom of
Aeneas — Aeneid X.606–688". ¶ units: 606 only (Greenough's single paragraph start in this part). make_units.py
prints no warnings. `sc` not written. PAIRS is empty (no split speech marks).

## Misprints (rule 5b)
- None found (checked every line for lowercase after a full stop, stray or unbalanced marks, odd letters).
- 661 `praelia`: taken as Greenough's spelling of `proelia` (noted once in n). I could not check whether he prints
  `praelia` elsewhere (the source file is outside the files I was allowed to read). If the edition has `proelia`
  everywhere else, the reviewer may want to treat this as a misprint under 5b instead.
- Kept as Greenough's spellings, noted: `adlacrimans`, `avolsam`, `rebare`, `pericli`, `tanton`, `Aenean`/`Aenea`;
  `adsimulat`, `inritat` not noted separately.

## Variants (Latin Library) and how handled
- 661–662 (`Illum autem Aeneas… morti`): Greenough after 660, Latin Library after 664. Greenough's order kept; the
  n of unit 661–662 says so (and that the LL order keeps the phantom's story unbroken).
- 673 `Quosne` / `quosque`: question with `-ne` vs. plain relative running on from 672. I judged the sense
  essentially the same but the construction different, and mentioned it in one clause of the n of 673. Reviewer
  may cut it as below the "changes the sense" bar.
- 660 `avolsamque`/`auulsamque` (orthography), 679 `neque`/`nec` (no change): not noted as variants.

## Segmentation
- 636–642 is one sentence of seven lines with only commas inside. Split at `euntis,` (636–640, five lines) and the
  simile 641–642; the n of 636 says the unit ends at a comma. This is the only unit ending in a comma (the 078
  ENDING check allows ','); reviewer should confirm this is acceptable house practice.
- 680–684 kept as one five-line unit (no internal stop; the `an… an` double question).
- Short units joined to neighbours: `conicit:` into 645–646; `Thalamos ne desere pactos;` with 650; `Vix proram
  attigerat:` with 660; `poscit;` with 662; `Quo feror? Unde abii? Quae… reducit?` as one unit; `Vos O potius
  miserescite venti:` with 677–679.

## Readings I am less than sure of
- 608 `ut rebare, Venus…`: taken as Jupiter's irony (Conington, I believe, reads it so; from memory).
- 625 `hactenus indulsisse vacat`: perfect infinitive taken in present sense ("there is room to indulge you so far").
- 630–631 `aut ego veri vana feror`: "or I go astray from the truth"; n also gives "perhaps 'I am said to be'".
- 660 `revoluta per aequora`: n leaves open ebb tide vs. water rolling back from the ship ("perhaps… perhaps").
- 670 `quemve reducit`: `quem` taken predicatively ("as what man", i.e. a deserter).
- 678 `Syrtis` taken as genitive singular ("of the Syrtis").
- 686 `animi` with `miserata`: genitive/locative of feeling; origin given as "perhaps".

## Attributions written from memory, not checked against a text
- Zeus and Hera over Sarpedon, Iliad 16.431–461.
- Apollo's image of Aeneas, Iliad 5.449–453; Apollo as Agenor luring Achilles, Iliad 21.595–605 (marked "perhaps").
- Earth gape for me: Agamemnon Iliad 4.182, Hector of Paris 6.281–282 (marked "perhaps"); Dido, Aen. IV.24.
- Achilles deliberating whether to draw on Agamemnon, Iliad 1.188–194 (marked "perhaps").
- Patroclus three times at the wall, Iliad 16.702–705 (marked "perhaps").
- Pilumnus an Italian god and Turnus's ancestor; Daunus king of Ardea; Ardea a few miles from the coast.
- Osinius named only here (marked "perhaps"); Clusium an inland Etruscan town.
- Lavinia promised by Latinus to Aeneas and claimed by Turnus (650).

## Advisory
- None recommended. 680–682 is Turnus weighing whether to fall on his sword: a thought, two lines, not carried out
  (Juno restrains him, 685–686), with no graphic detail. The n of 680 says plainly "fall on his sword"; no
  softening. If the owner decides suicide (QUESTIONS, Dido) should carry an advisory even when only contemplated,
  this part would be borderline; I judge it below the bar.
